test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Identify the meaning of the phrase highlighted in bold.

The mode of payment is cash is a __**pain in the neck**__ for those who have no habit of carrying cash around them.

options.text: When something is not up to the mark

solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. When someone/something is very annoying .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**pain in the neck**" is a commonly used idiom in English that refers to someone or something that is very annoying or causes inconvenience.
 
• In the given sentence, "The mode of payment is cash is a pain in the neck for those who have no habit of carrying cash around them," the phrase is used to express how inconvenient it is for people who do not carry cash to make payments in cash.
 
• Among the options provided, **Option 4: "When someone/something is very annoying"** correctly describes the meaning of the phrase.

Correct interpretation: *The phrase "pain in the neck" means something that is very annoying or inconvenient.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Idioms related to inconvenience or annoyance:**

 
 
• **A thorn in one’s side:** Something or someone that continuously causes problems or annoyance.
 
• **Drive someone up the wall:** To make someone extremely annoyed or frustrated.
 
 
 
• **Usage:**
 
 
• Idioms like "pain in the neck" are often used in informal contexts to describe frustrating situations or people.
 
• Example: "Having to redo the entire project was a real pain in the neck."
